reviewScope: Physical registration only. Reviewed entries have individually inspected roots; pending entries remain unused by normalization. No artistic acceptance or runtime integration.

enemy-031-dust-runner.method: Manual per-pose visual inspection of the pelvis center immediately ahead of the tail base at the proximal hind-leg joint, projected vertically to observed paw/body support. The support coordinate includes the complete extracted source lower bound and guard pixel, so sourceBounds[3] - anchorY must be <= 0 for every pose. Airborne pounce poses use an explicit ground plane inferred from adjacent grounded poses so flight height is preserved. Whole-body bounding boxes and tail extrema are never used as the landmark.
enemy-031-dust-runner.visualReview: All 32 source poses and four marked root contacts were inspected. Idle border clues at frames 4 and 7 are single bright-magenta corner pixels, not anatomy; default extraction passes without safe reassignment. Registration only, not scale application, loop approval or runtime acceptance.

enemy-033-arcology-lurker.method: Manual whole-board review on a 25 px nominal-cell grid. The anatomical landmark is the visually stable ventral ribcage center and is unchanged by this correction. The physical root shares its x coordinate and projects vertically to the observed load-bearing paw/digit support line, then adds the complete four-pixel extraction margin so anchorY equals sourceBounds[3] in every pose. Tail-tip extrema are excluded. Death uses the corpse contact plane. Attack frame 2 uses the authored action plane at the lowest distal limb because the torso is airborne. This is standalone physical-registration evidence, not runtime acceptance.

enemy-037-neomorph.method: Manual per-frame review in original 1774x887 4x2 source coordinates. The landmark is the visible pelvis/posterior hip articulation at the sacral tail root, never the tail tip, skull, hand or global bounding-box centre. Anchor x is the landmark's vertical projection. Anchor y equals the complete recovered sourceBounds bottom, including the full three-pixel extraction guard below the load-bearing feet, knees, hands, forearms or corpse flank. The attack frame-2 negative x bound is retained exactly after the separately proven safe ownership transfer; it does not alter pelvis or ground placement.

Physical registration only; no artistic acceptance, scale merge, normalization or runtime integration.
